Summary

Restore the welcome-back header message that appears when a returning user has their profile restored.

Background

The previous header showed a short message such as: "Welcome back, [name]! Your profile has been successfully restored." In the new header design, this message no longer appears, so returning users do not get clear confirmation that their profile was restored.

Expected behavior

  • Show the welcome-back message at the top of the header when the user is marked as returning.
  • Let users dismiss the message.
  • Hide the message automatically after a short period.
  • Keep the header layout stable after the message appears or closes.
  • Avoid server-side rendering errors when the message state changes.

Notes

This should match the new header design while bringing back the previous user-facing behavior.

QA Tester Summary — Issue #1713

Verdict: ✅ Passed
Environment: Dev https://dev.villume.com · real tester-account restoration flow
Suite: qa_testing/tests/e2e/header/issue_1713_welcome_back_header.spec.ts (Playwright · Chromium) — passed
Runtime evidence: Manual real-site verification by the user confirmed the returning-user banner appears after the account was deleted and logged in again. No automated screenshot/video was attached because the agent-run browser session did not reproduce the transient banner state.

Test summary

# Method Scenario Expected result Evidence Result
1 White box Header consumes userInfo.is_back, renders the message and close control Returning state produces the specified message and a dismiss action Source review + rerunnable suite ✅ Pass
2 Gray box Header marks the returning state handled and schedules auto-dismiss State update occurs; timeout is 30 seconds; close flow resets the message Source review + rerunnable suite ✅ Pass
3 Black box A restored tester account logs in on the real Dev site Banner is visible at the top of the header and can be dismissed User manual real-site test ✅ Pass
4 Black box Regular unauthenticated profile request Protected endpoint rejects an anonymous request Automated API assertion: HTTP 401 UNAUTHENTICATED ✅ Pass
5 Confusion matrix Positive restored-user case / negative anonymous case Banner shown only for the restored-user condition; protected API rejects anonymous access User manual test + automated assertion TP + TN ✅

Code review

Area Review result
Returning-user condition syncHeaderMessageVisibility() guards on userInfo?.is_back.
Banner copy and UI The exact welcome-back message and accessible close button are implemented in the header.
Dismiss and timeout The banner invokes updateUserIsBack(), supports manual close, and auto-closes after 30 seconds.
SSR safety Browser-only DOM work is guarded by isPlatformBrowser().

Evidence and limitations

  • Agent-run automated suite: 1 passed.
  • Real runtime result: supplied and manually verified by the user after delete → login again.
  • No coding bug was confirmed.

Summary

Tidy the header menu styling so the header and menu behavior are easier to maintain.

Background

The header menu styles had grown across component and shared styling areas. This made it harder to understand which styles controlled the visible menu and increased the risk of layout regressions.

Expected behavior

  • Keep the header menu visually consistent with the current design.
  • Keep desktop and mobile header behavior stable.
  • Move shared menu styling to the appropriate shared styling area.
  • Use clearer class names for the menu styling.
  • Keep existing header tests aligned with the updated markup.

Notes

This should preserve the current header experience while making future menu styling changes safer.

Summary

Improve the avatar upload preview so it renders as a normal image.

Background

The avatar preview was using background-image styling to show the selected image. Rendering the preview as an image is clearer and easier to maintain, and better matches how users expect image previews to behave.

Expected behavior

  • Show the avatar preview as an image element.
  • Preserve the current preview appearance.
  • Keep upload and preview behavior unchanged for users.
  • Remove code that only existed to support the old preview approach.

Notes

This is a small cleanup to make the avatar preview implementation simpler without changing the user-facing flow.

Summary

Clean up old scrollbar styling and use a simpler styling approach.

Background

Some scrollbar styling relied on browser-specific rules. This adds unnecessary maintenance cost and can behave inconsistently across browsers.

Expected behavior

  • Remove outdated browser-specific scrollbar styling where it is no longer needed.
  • Keep scrolling behavior working normally.
  • Preserve the current layout and usability.
  • Prefer simpler styling that is easier to maintain across browsers.

Notes

This should reduce styling complexity without changing how users interact with scrollable areas.
